findings.reason: Alternating forward/backward lunge steps are a dynamic bodyweight movement; nothing is held isometrically against an external load.
tracking_type is bodyweight_reps and bodyweight=true, so there is no external load to enter; total_load contradicts it.
Unloaded bodyweight movement: performance depends on bodyweight, so bodyweight_aware, not cross-gym 'exercise'.
bodyweight=true and the load is the trainee's own body leaning against a surface; 'gravity' is used elsewhere for external implements.

With a dumbbell held by the feet the resistance moment arm about the knee is maximal at full knee extension (lengthened) and goes to zero as the shin approaches vertical (shortened). Stored profile is inverted.
Description explicitly says 'dumbbells are pulled towards the chest' - a bilateral two-dumbbell row; side_mode 'separate' follows the same wrong premise.
Description says 'Bilateral dumbbell row' and the name says two-arm.
A side plank with a rear fly is performed on one side at a time with one loaded arm; it cannot be bilateral.

In a bent-over kickback the dumbbell moment arm about the elbow is near zero with the forearm hanging (lengthened) and maximal with the arm extended back (shortened). Stored profile is inverted; this is the archetypal shortened-biased triceps movement.
Description says 'Lifting dumbbells towards the chin' - the standard bilateral upright row.
Description says 'Unilateral press of a barbell fixed in a landmine attachment'; side_mode 'none' compounds it.
A standing stretch with no equipment rows and resistance from body position only; comparable stretches in the catalogue are bodyweight=true.
The floor press exists precisely to remove the need for a spotter: range is limited by the floor and a single kettlebell can be dropped to the side safely.
Conditioning jump with no external load; resistance_source is already bodyweight_leverage and no equipment is linked.
Description and resistance_source (cam_machine) say the load comes from a neck machine weight stack, not from bodyweight.
Machine neck flexion is a plain weight x reps exercise; there is no bodyweight component to add to.
Neck machines differ per model; loads are not comparable across gyms and are not bodyweight-dependent.

The archer push-up shifts most of the load onto one arm and demands significant unilateral pressing strength and scapular control - and this variant adds external weight. 'low' contradicts the movement.
The load is bodyweight plus added weight on the back; comparison_scope is already bodyweight_aware, which weight_reps/total_load contradicts.
Description is a static hold at lockout; there are no repetitions to count. Duration under load is the measured quantity.
The resistance is a weight hanging from the roller cord; nothing about the exercise is bodyweight-loaded.
Follows from the bodyweight error: the wrist roller is loaded only by the hanging plate.

non_vocabulary_findings.problem: exercise_muscle lists rectus_abdominis as the only 'primary' muscle of a 400 m sprint, with quadriceps and gastrocnemius demoted to secondary. The prime movers of sprinting are the hip extensors (gluteus maximus, hamstrings) and knee extensors; the abdominals are trunk stabilizers.
kinetic_chain='closed' but the moving leg is free in the air (hips on the ball, foot unsupported). By the clinical definition the distal segment is not fixed, so this is open chain.
exercise_equipment links 'treadmill' to an upper-body arm ergometer. The described implement is an arm/hand bike ergometer, not a treadmill.
kinetic_chain='open' for a barbell back squat. The feet are fixed on the floor and the body moves around them - the textbook closed-chain exercise.

No exercise_equipment rows although the description is a chin-up performed on a bar; every other chin-up/pull-up in the sample links pull_up_bar. Presented as an equipment-free exercise it cannot be performed.
No exercise_equipment rows although the exercise is defined by a ski ergometer; the machine is the exercise.

Joint actions store shoulder.horizontal_adduction as primary and movement pattern horizontal_press as primary for a bench/parallel dip. A dip is shoulder extension plus elbow extension (vertical press) - the parallel-bar dip in the same sample is coded exactly that way, so this one contradicts both the movement and its own catalogue.
No exercise_equipment rows although the name and description specify a strap.

Two problems: kinetic_chain='open' while the athlete hangs from a fixed bar (hands fixed, body moves = closed), and the muscle list contains only biceps/brachialis/forearms with no latissimus dorsi or teres major, although the front lever curl is driven by shoulder extension against the lats.
